title: How to Generate Mergeable Code with a Context Engine — Peter Werry, Unblocked
talk_summary: Unblocked pitches a 'context engine' that pre-distills organizational context (PR history, Slack decisions, architecture docs, expertise graph) and serves task-specific slices to agents instead of dumping the whole repo or letting them search blindly. The concrete, copyable claims are: pre-built per-task context cuts token spend and loop count, and surfacing prior reviewer comments/expertise into a review agent improves review signal.

takeaways.technique: Pre-distilled task-scoped context pack instead of agent self-search
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a context layer that ingests PRs, Slack, docs, and architecture rationale, then assembles a task-specific context bundle with cited sources so the agent starts with the right facts rather than searching.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the real value of a context engine is not like the upfront cost on these short tasks. It's the compounding effect
takeaways.numbers: ~1 min and sub-$1 to produce a plan with context vs ~2 min and higher cost without

takeaways.technique: Surface prior human review comments as review-agent priors
takeaways.what_they_do: Feed historical PR review comments into the review agent, weighted by reviewer seniority, so it echoes and applies established team standards rather than generic lint.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it surfaced the uh the previous comments. Richie's one of the senior engineers and we use the sort of seniority or expertise as a signal

takeaways.what_they_do: Every context-engine answer returns the source documents it used, so humans (and downstream agents) can verify and jump to the source to correct the knowledge base.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it shows its work and this is really important because um all of these things here the sources come back to Claude and then Claude knows exactly where to jump to next

takeaways.what_they_do: Argue against stuffing the full codebase/docs into the window because it distracts the agent and wastes tokens; instead give only task-relevant context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it causes the agent to get distracted. When you're working on a task, you want task specific flow

takeaways.technique: Engineering social graph / expertise map for routing and coverage
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a graph of who reviews whose code to identify expertise clusters and coverage gaps, and use it to weight review comments and route work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can then cluster that and generate team labels for that or show the coverage across your codebase
